question: Can normal SIGTERM stop and ownership-bound socket cleanup prevent retained supervisor sockets without deleting retained or replaced paths?
baseline: No SIGTERM handler; finally unlinks any socket path and startup auto-unlinks root-owned socket.
acceptance: Original real-subprocess SIGTERM regression leaves socket; corrected subprocess exits and removes only its bound inode.
Preserve existing startup and replaced sockets, regular files and symlinks.
Terminate launched process group during unwind and reap the direct child within service stop budget.
Existing browser tests continue to pass.
limits: UID1000 local tests double root identity/chown only; no OCI service qualification.
SIGKILL cannot run Python cleanup; strict reconciliation remains required.
Path identity check plus unlink is not an atomic conditional-unlink primitive against a privileged concurrent namespace writer.
